body:
Conclusion: the host-contract version that applies to this workspace's integration is generation 1 (HOST_CONTRACT_VERSION = 1), asserted at assembly via assertHostContract(1). Matching is exact and fail-closed — any other value throws HostContractMismatchError (HOST_CONTRACT_MISMATCH) at createPalimpsestEffects assembly, and there is no tolerance layer/shim.

Load-bearing evidence (local, co-applicable):
1. Pinned shipped contract — node_modules/@ordarium/core (package version 1.3.1) dist/src/host.js declares `export const HOST_CONTRACT_VERSION = 1`, and assertHostContract() throws unless the caller's literal equals it. @ordarium/host-kit 1.3.1 is a curated re-export of this constant from core (node_modules/@ordarium/host-kit/dist/src/index.js), so the handshake the workspace imports resolves to that value.
2. Workspace assembly — src/effects/runtime.ts:128 calls `assertHostContract(1)` inside createPalimpsestEffects, commented as "the host-contract generation palimpsest was built and tested against, pinned as a literal — a contract bump fails closed at assembly."
3. Test — test/host_conformance.test.ts CONF-A01 asserts assertHostContract(1) passes and assertHostContract(2) throws HostContractMismatchError.
4. Spec — docs/engineering/13-host-adapter-conformance-spec.md §0/§1.1/§2/§3: G18 delivered contract generation 1; literal 1 pinned; mismatch = fail-closed, no compatibility layer. docs/engineering/07-ordarium-alignment.md r19 records no HOST_CONTRACT_VERSION→2 plan on either side.

Apparent conflicts examined and resolved by scope:
- package.json and pnpm-workspace.yaml pin the @ordarium/* release line at 1.3.1 (four tarball URLs), while historical records (docs/07, docs/13, docker/minimal/README.md, README.md, audits) still say 1.2.0. That is the package release version axis, not the host-contract generation axis. The 1.2.0 records are the conformance-era milestone (2026-09-06/07) and reflect the then-current release; the currently installed/authoritative artifact is 1.3.1. Both lines expose contract generation 1 (docs/13 §0 states G18 delivered contract generation 1; the installed 1.3.1 artifact confirms HOST_CONTRACT_VERSION = 1), so the proposition is co-applicable and resolves to 1. The stale release-pin wording is documentation drift, not a second contract generation.
- docs/engineering/11-superseded-interface-note.md is explicitly marked SUPERSEDED/void, is not registered in the docs/engineering/README index, and carries no version of its own: it defers to "the pinned dependency's shipped contract," i.e. the 1.3.1 artifact above. It cannot be read as a competing source.
- Only one HOST_CONTRACT_VERSION definition exists anywhere in the workspace (core dist, = 1); no contract v2 artifact is present.

No peer consultation was needed: the authoritative value ships inside the locally pinned dependency artifact and every load-bearing local source agrees on generation 1; the only residual difference (1.2.0 vs 1.3.1) concerns the package release pin in historical records and is settled by version/temporal scope.
